rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for coughing, especially when no expelled substance is specified.

example.english: I cough a lot these days.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ni1 gei2 jat6 seng4 jat6 kat1

rows.note: Use this when specifying that something is coughed out of the lungs or throat, such as blood or phlegm.

example.english: When I cough up phlegm, I spit it out.
example.traditional: 我咳出嚟啲痰，就吐咗佢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 kat1 ceot1 lei4 di1 taam4 zau6 tou3 zo2 keoi5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual noun for a single cough or cough sound.

example.english: I just heard someone cough behind me.
example.traditional: 我啱啱聽到後面有人咳咗一聲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ngaam1 ngaam1 teng1 dou2 hau6 min6 jau5 jan4 kat1 zo2 jat1 sing1

rows.note: Use this for a bout of coughing or the medical symptom or condition causing it.

example.english: I've had a bad cough lately, and I can't sleep at night.
example.traditional: 我呢排成日咳嗽，夜晚都瞓唔到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ni1 paai4 seng4 jat6 kat1 sau3 je6 maan5 dou1 fan3 m4 dou2
